title: Woman sues Court TV over release of her name in Irish firefighter rape case
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Woman sues Court TV for $2.8 million, claiming they revealed her identity during a rape retrial.
Court TV allegedly showed the victim's name during live broadcast and on social media, violating legal protections.
The incident reportedly worsened the woman's mental health and required additional therapy and medication.

title: Healey signs sweeping law to restrict ICE
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed the PROTECT Act to restrict ICE activities in Massachusetts, affecting schools and hospitals.
The law prohibits warrantless immigration arrests in specific locations and allows parents to pre-arrange guardianship during deportation.
The PROTECT Act immediately enforces a state civil rights claim for residents against government officials violating constitutional rights.

title: Here’s how Mass. hospitals fared in the latest U.S. News rankings
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Massachusetts General and Brigham and Women's Hospitals ranked in the nationwide top 20 U.S. News honor roll.
Dana-Farber Brigham Cancer Center ranked third nationally for cancer care in U.S. News rankings.
Beth Israel Deaconess and Lahey Clinic ranked third and fourth among the best hospitals in Massachusetts.

title: Stefon Diggs reportedly ‘set to sign’ with Commanders on one-year deal
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Stefon Diggs set to sign a one-year contract with the Washington Commanders; deal worth up to $12 million.
Diggs caught 85 passes for 1,013 yards and four touchdowns in 2025 with the New England Patriots.
Diggs, 32, was found not guilty of felony strangulation and misdemeanor assault charges in May 2026.

title: Patriots teammates believe Will Campbell is ready for Year 2 jump
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots left tackle Will Campbell aims for significant improvements in his second NFL season after a challenging rookie year.
Veteran Dre'Mont Jones praises Campbell's progress, noting his stronger, smarter play during New England's training camp.
Quarterback Drake Maye and teammates express confidence in Campbell's ability to excel in the upcoming 2026 season.

title: Snag one-way fares for as low as $54 during JetBlue’s fall travel flash sale
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: JetBlue launched a 48-hour flash sale on fall flights, with one-way domestic fares starting at $54 and transatlantic at $299.
The sale applies to travel between Sept. 9 and Nov. 18, excluding blackout dates Oct. 9-14 and Nov. 8-11.
JetBlue's new fare options include BlueFirst, its upcoming domestic first-class, alongside Main, EvenMore, and Mint experiences.

title: Moulton doubles down on Epstein-related attacks on Markey
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Rep. Seth Moulton accused Sen. Ed Markey of being involved in Jeffrey Epstein's lobbying efforts during a recent debate.
Moulton shared images on social media allegedly linking Markey to Epstein, despite Markey's denial of any connection.
Evidence shows Markey met colleagues of an Epstein-associated lobbyist regarding Senegal politics, but no direct Epstein link.

title: New Red Sox reliever Erik Miller says he learned about trade from TV
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Erik Miller learned of his trade to the Red Sox from a TV announcement, feeling shocked but excited.
Miller struck out the only batter he faced in his debut for Boston against the White Sox.
Miller was previously with the Giants and joins the Red Sox bullpen with a 2.14 ERA over 75 appearances.

title: ‘Sheer grit and determination’: Mass. 18-year-old with leg injury meets rescuers halfway on Mount Washington
author: John Waller
bullets: Andrew Nelson, 18, from Topsfield, injured his leg a half-mile from Mount Washington's summit on Tuesday afternoon.
Rescue teams responded after a 911 call; Nelson hiked 0.3 miles using assistance from friends and determination.
Rescuers applied a vacuum splint and carried him 0.2 miles; Nelson declined hospital transport, seeking home treatment.

title: Body washes up at Orient Heights Beach in East Boston
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A female body was discovered around 1 p.m. Tuesday at Orient Heights Beach, East Boston.
The body was found near Bayswater Street, according to the Suffolk County District Attorney's Office.
An investigation into the incident is ongoing, and further updates are anticipated soon.
